outgoing.name: Canada
outgoing.excerpt: They also celebrate and promote a National Elizabeth Fry Week in Canada each May.

outgoing.name: England
outgoing.excerpt: Elizabeth Fry (née Gurney; 21 May 1780 – 12 October 1845) was an English prison reformer, social reformer and philanthropist.

outgoing.name: London
outgoing.excerpt: Fry also helped the homeless, establishing a "nightly shelter" in London after seeing the body of a young boy in the winter of 1819/ 1820.

outgoing.name: Norwich
outgoing.excerpt: In February 2007 a new plaque was placed in her honour on the Friends Meeting House in Upper Goat Lane, Norwich.

outgoing.name: Ramsgate
outgoing.excerpt: Fry died at Ramsgate on 13 October 1845 and her remains were buried in the Friends' burial ground at Barking.

outgoing.name: Religious Society of Friends
outgoing.excerpt: Elizabeth Gurney was born in Gurney Court, off Magdalen Street, Norwich, Norfolk, England to a Quaker family.

outgoing.name: Society
outgoing.excerpt: Fry became well known in society.

outgoing.name: Weymouth
outgoing.excerpt: Thomas Fowell Buxton, Fry's brother-in-law, was elected to Parliament for Weymouth and began to promote her work among his fellow MPs.
